compiler-contract.description: Defines compiler behavior for source resolution, contract validation, interaction state generation, gamut routing, and design tool handoff.
source-resolution-order: 1. Check layer-2 semantic-mapping for the role name
2. Read the source field from that role
3. If source ends in -greyscale: resolve against layer-1 greyscale-outputs
4. If source is a semantic role name: recurse through semantic-mapping
5. If source is a layer-1 hue-family name: resolve directly against layer-1 hue-families
6. If source cannot be resolved: trigger on-contract-violation

hue-family-resolution-reference.description: Hue family classification is formally defined in Layer 3 under hue-family-resolution. All compiler steps MUST use that definition.
hue-family-resolution-reference.divergence-prevention: One authoritative mapping. Do not implement a local override.

hue-distance-math-requirement.rule: min(abs(a - b), 360 - abs(a - b)) for all hue proximity checks.
hue-distance-math-requirement.rationale: Hue is circular. Linear abs() fails at 0°/360° boundary.
hue-distance-math-requirement.failure-mode-if-violated: Conflicting colours near boundary pass guardrails silently.

handoff-routing.description: Routes gamut-specific token values to different consumer environments. Resolves the conflict between design intent (P3) and engineering safety (sRGB).

validation-check.description: Emit dual variants only when P3 and sRGB values actually differ.
validation-check.instruction: If abs(C_p3 - C_srgb) < 0.001 for a stop, it is sRGB-safe — emit one token.

design-tool-target.figma-instruction: Set Figma file to Display P3 color profile before importing. File > Color Profile > Display P3.
design-tool-target.compiler-instruction: Base $value MUST be un-clamped P3 hex. sRGB emitted as secondary variable suffixed -srgb-fallback.

css-output-pattern.hdr-block: @media (color-gamut: p3) and (dynamic-range: high) { --color-{role}: oklch(var(--{role}-l) var(--{role}-c-hdr) var(--{role}-h)); }

engineering-target.compiler-instruction: Base CSS value MUST be sRGB-clamped. P3 values route exclusively into @media (color-gamut: p3) blocks. HDR values route into combined @media (color-gamut: p3) and (dynamic-range: high) blocks.
engineering-target.react-native-note: React Native does not support @media (color-gamut). Emit sRGB only for React Native targets.

gamut-tiers.description: Three-tier progressive gamut system. Architecture supports HDR now even if HDR token values match P3 initially.

handoff-routing.audit-requirement: Build report must log which tokens required dual variants and which were sRGB-safe.

apca-extensions-policy.description: Governs which tokens require $extensions.org.design-system.apca blocks and how the compiler enforces them.
apca-extensions-policy.gamut-requirement-note: Both srgb and p3 gamuts must be tested for any token marked as dual-variant.
apca-extensions-policy.re-audit-trigger: Any $value change sets verified=false on that token. Build fails until audit tool re-runs and resets verified=true.
apca-extensions-policy.invalidation-rule: verified and lc fields must not be hand-edited. They are write-once by the audit tool only.

fail-build.behavior: Halt. Print role, source, resolution path.

warn-and-continue.behavior: Emit warning. Substitute #FF00FF as visible fallback.

interaction-state-method.approach: lightness-delta and chroma-delta in OKLCH space via layer-3 delta-engine
interaction-state-method.why-not-stop-index: Stop +100 jumps are not perceptually uniform across hue families.
interaction-state-method.delta-values-source: layer-3 delta-engine state-delta-rules — single source of truth.

compiler-contract.semantic-layer-purity-rule: Interaction-tokens and mode-mapping must only reference semantic role names. Never layer-1 hue-family names directly.

overlay-token-contract.description: Governs how overlay tokens (semi-transparent fills used for scrims, image tints, selection highlights) are defined, resolved, and output. Overlay tokens alias a solid primitive and add an alpha channel at the semantic layer — primitives remain 100% solid at all times.
syntax-examples: {pg.900} @ 26%  — dark modal backdrop in light mode
{pg.50} @ 26%   — light modal backdrop in dark mode
{primary.900} @ 15% — brand tint over imagery in light mode

cross-wiring-rule.description: Overlay tokens are intentionally cross-wired between light and dark modes. In light mode a dark stop is used to create a receding tint. In dark mode a light stop is used to maintain equivalent visual weight.

css-output.why-color-mix: color-mix preserves the perceptual colour identity of the primitive in OKLCH space. Direct oklch() with alpha channel is equivalent but requires decomposed L/C/H variables to be available.
css-output.browser-support: color-mix(in oklch) requires Chrome 111+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.2+. Emit a solid hex fallback for older environments.

figma-output.instruction: In Figma Variables, alias the semantic overlay variable to its solid primitive. Once the alias is set, type the opacity percentage into the opacity box next to the alias — do NOT create a new solid colour with baked-in alpha. The opacity is scoped to the semantic variable only. The primitive remains 100% solid.
figma-output.why: If the primitive hue is updated later, the overlay automatically inherits the new hue while retaining its opacity. Baking alpha into the primitive hex breaks this chain.
figma-output.tokens-studio-note: Tokens Studio supports opacity on alias references via the 'opacity' modifier field.

apca-prohibition.rule: Text tokens MUST NEVER be placed directly on an overlay token background.
apca-prohibition.reason: APCA computes contrast between two resolved colours. An overlay token has no resolved background — it inherits whatever is beneath it at runtime (photo, gradient, another component). The contrast ratio is undefined at token-authoring time and cannot be guaranteed.
apca-prohibition.compiler-enforcement: If any component token pairs a text role with an overlay role as its background, the compiler must emit a HARD BUILD ERROR — not a warning.
apca-prohibition.error-message: OVERLAY_TEXT_PAIR: '{text-token}' is paired with overlay token '{overlay-token}'. Text must never be placed on an overlay background. Pair text with a solid surface role instead.

valid-use-cases: modal-backdrop — scrim behind a dialog. Text sits on the solid dialog surface, not the scrim.
image-tint — brand or semantic colour wash over a thumbnail or hero image.
selection-highlight — list item or text selection at <= 8% opacity. At this opacity the underlying solid surface contrast ratio is not meaningfully impacted.
drop-zone-highlight — brand tint over a drag target area.
invalid-use-cases: text-background — any token that text is placed directly on top of.
button-fill — buttons need solid fills for guaranteed contrast.
input-fill — form fields need solid fills for guaranteed contrast.
card-surface — surfaces that host content must be solid.

opacity-guidelines.selection-highlight: 5–8%. Above 8% may impact underlying text contrast.

checks: 1. Resolve the base primitive alias — must be a valid solid primitive stop.
2. Opacity must be a number 1–99. 0% and 100% are errors — use transparent or solid token instead.
3. No component text token may reference this overlay token as its background pair.
4. Emit dual variants (P3/sRGB) for the base hex per handoff-routing rules. Apply opacity to both variants.
5. Log all overlay tokens in build report with their base hex, opacity, and use-case field.

apca-role-targets.description: Per semantic-role Lc targets. Prefix-matched, first match wins. Replaces the flat Lc 60 used for all text roles. Caption/overline at 12px need Lc 90. Display text at 60px+ can use Lc 45. A flat threshold is a false guarantee at small sizes.
apca-role-targets.scientific-basis: APCA is spatial-frequency aware. Required contrast scales with font size and weight. Lc 60 is correct for ui-label context (>=18px, regular weight). It is dangerously low for caption/overline and unnecessarily strict for display text.

targets.rationale: Caption is always 12-13px. Small-field tritanopia risk. Highest contrast required.
Overline is always 11-12px. Same as caption.
Label at 13-14px. Body-text contrast needed at small size.
Running text requires Lc 75 for sustained reading comfort.
Primary text is body reading text.
Secondary text: supplementary, shorter runs. Lc 60 acceptable.
Disabled: intentionally low contrast per APCA spec.
Display text is 60px+. Large format allows lower Lc.
Default text target for unlisted text roles.
Icon contrast. Small icons (<16px) should target Lc 60.

surface-chroma-policy.description: Surface/bg/subtle tokens must not appear self-luminous (emissive). High chroma at mid-lightness creates a glowing appearance that breaks material metaphor.
surface-chroma-policy.compiler-check: STEP 9f in compiler. Emits warning — not a hard error.

cvd-guardrail-reference.description: CVD simulation check is defined in Layer 3 cvd-guardrail-policy. Layer 2 registers the pairs to check.

changelog.1.8: Added apca-role-targets (per-role Lc targets replacing flat 60). Added power-curve elevation params. Added surface-chroma-policy and cvd-guardrail-reference.

semantic-mapping.description: Maps semantic role names to layer-1 hue-family sources and stop positions. All role names are the contract between design and engineering.

text-secondary.stop-rationale: Stop 700 on primary-greyscale gives Lc 42 on background (stop 50) — fails APCA ui-label minimum of Lc 60. Stop 800 (#373239) gives estimated Lc 68. Corrected per apca-extensions-audit-policy known-failures log.

semantic-conflict-guardrails.auto-shift-policy: false — emit warnings, require human resolution.
semantic-conflict-guardrails.override-instructions: To acknowledge a conflict and allow the build to proceed, add an entry to known-exceptions. The 'primary-hex-reviewed' field is REQUIRED and must exactly match the current primary hex in Layer 1 brand-inputs. If the primary hex changes, the override is automatically invalidated and the hard stop fires again — forcing a fresh review. This prevents stale sign-offs from silently accepting new conflicts.

known-exceptions.rationale: Brand primary is intentionally golden-orange. We rely on iconography to distinguish warnings.

semantic-conflict-guardrails.hex-binding-rule: The compiler checks primary-hex-reviewed against the current Layer 1 primary hex at build time. If they differ the override is REJECTED and the hard stop fires. Changing the brand primary hex always requires a fresh review.

success.stop-rationale: True-green family at stop 500 fails Lc 60 on white (Lc 51.2). Stop 600 (#007E00) gives Lc 71.6 on white (passes ui-label) and Lc 75.7 with on-success (passes body text). Corrected per APCA audit.

warning.stop-rationale: Orange family at stop 500 fails Lc 60 on white (high luminance hue). Stop 700 required to meet ui-components Lc 45 minimum on white backgrounds.

focus-ring-tokens.description: Emitted as separate tokens. Subject to dual-variant rule if source hue requires P3.
focus-ring-tokens.dark-mode-note: Focus ring color must be re-verified for Lc against dark-mode surface stops in mode-mapping.

computed-tokens.description: First-class primitive ramp. Resolved via primitive-token-naming.ramp-keys.elev. Keys '0'–'4' match {elev.N} pattern. Recomputed when dark-mode-config.floor-stop changes.
computed-tokens.power-curve-note: Weber-Fechner law correction (concern #20). Linear ΔL steps feel unequal: early levels too similar, late levels too separated. Power curve: L(i) = FLOOR_L + ((i/4)^1.3) × total-dL. Steps: 0→1: 0.015, 1→2: 0.018, 2→3: 0.021, 3→4: 0.026. Early steps smaller (reduces Mach Band artefacts at base). Late steps larger (more distinct elevation at dialog/sheet level). Total range preserved at 0.08 matching previous 4 × 0.02.

dark-mode-elevation.base-L: derived at compile time from floor-stop
dark-mode-elevation.correction-note: Elevation tokens are now fully derived from dark-mode-config.floor-stop. No hardcoded base. Designer changes floor-stop once; compiler regenerates all elevation tokens automatically.
dark-mode-elevation.primitive-promotion-note: elev is a first-class primitive ramp registered in layer-1 primitive-token-naming.ramp-keys. {elev.N} aliases resolve through the same path as {pg.N}, {primary.N} etc. — no special handling needed.

mode-mapping.alias-note: Values are DTCG alias references. {pg.*} = primary-greyscale ramp stops. {elev.*} = dark-mode elevation computed tokens (layer-2 mode-mapping.dark-mode-elevation.computed-tokens). Raw hex must never be substituted here.

dark-mode-config.description: Designer-controlled dark mode floor. Change floor-stop to any valid stop in valid-floor-stops. The compiler reads this value and derives all elevation tokens and dark-mode surface aliases automatically. No other changes needed.

valid-floor-stops-guide.950: Standard dark mode (L 0.17). Near-black ergonomic surfaces (18.6:1 glare vs white, IBM Carbon / M3 standard). Suitable for most dark UIs.
valid-floor-stops-guide.900: Medium dark mode (L 0.20). Charcoal surfaces. Good for editorial or accessible dark themes.
valid-floor-stops-guide.800: Light dark mode (L 0.30). Slate surfaces. Suitable for low-contrast dark themes.
valid-floor-stops-guide.700: Very light dark mode (L 0.40). Used when dark mode is more of a tinted neutral than a true dark surface.

compiler-instruction: 2. Look up floor-stop L value from Layer 1 lightness-behavior standard shadows
3. Look up the next coarser ramp stop L value (floor-stop - 1 level up the ramp)
4. Compute elevation stops using power curve: L(i) = floor_L + ((i/4)^power-curve-exponent) × total-dL. See dark-mode-elevation.computed-tokens.power-curve-exponent and total-dL.
5. Derive elev.0 through elev.4 hex values from those computed L values using pg C and H
6. All mode-mapping dark-mode surface aliases ({elev.0}–{elev.4}) resolve from these derived tokens
7. If floor-stop changes, ALL elevation tokens recompute automatically — no other edits needed

oled-reserved.note: pg.1000 is not part of the elevation ramp. It is an optional override for OLED displays only and requires an explicit product decision.

light-mode-cvd-rationale.description: Light mode semantic state fills are intentionally split in lightness (success at L~0.612 vs error at L~0.488) to ensure CVD distinction across deuteranopia and protanopia.
light-mode-cvd-rationale.structural-note: Guarantees that red and green never collapse to identical luminance in light mode, protecting ~8% of male users without compromising 100% WCAG AA compliance.

dark-mode-cvd-rationale.description: Dark mode semantic state stops are intentionally offset by 2 stops to ensure CVD lightness separation.
dark-mode-cvd-rationale.structural-note: This offset is hex-agnostic. It works because CVD simulation collapses chromatic channels, leaving only lightness as a differentiator. 2-stop separation at this region of the ramp guarantees ΔE > 0.10 for any hue.
